title: Lesson 19 - Embedding FlexCards: Component, Tab, and Console Placement
description: Prescribe the optimal placement and methods for embedding Flexcards within Salesforce (e.g., component, tab, console view) to meet strategic user enablement goals.

questions.question: A card shows data for the specific record the user is viewing. What is the best placement?
options: A tab with no record anchor
A Lightning component on the record page
questions.explanation: A card whose value depends on the record context belongs on the record page as a Lightning component, where it is bound to the record. A tab, utility panel, or dashboard has no record anchor, so the card would have to source its own context and would not automatically follow the record.

questions.question: A card shows cross-record aggregate data for managers. What is the best placement?
options: A Lightning component on a single record page
A tab that gives the card its own space
A card bound to a case record
questions.explanation: Cross-record aggregate data is not anchored to one record, so a tab placement that gives the card its own space is best. A record-page component or a case-bound card would anchor it to a single record, and a console view is for task-driven agent work, not a manager's aggregate view.

questions.question: A service agent resolves cases in the console and needs a card that supports that task. What is the best placement?
options: A tab the agent rarely opens
A console view placement alongside the workspace
A record page for a different object
questions.explanation: A task-driven card for an agent belongs in the console view, where the agent already works. A tab the agent rarely opens, a manager dashboard, or a record page for a different object would not put the card where the agent acts.
